Subject: Sealed-enclave private deployment: residency & SIG/CAIQ evidence request

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking the time on the call last week. Calyx is evaluating a private deployment of Redwood in a sealed-enclave configuration for a new regulated workload. Before we progress to procurement, our security team needs a compact evidence packet that covers the following items specific to the US-sealed-enclave setup:

- Short statement confirming data-at-rest residency in US-only nodes for the sealed-enclave deployment and controls for preventing cross-region KV cache & snapshot replication.
- Current SOC 2 Type II report (redacted OK) and a CAIQ / SIG condensed response focused on networking, key management, and access controls.
- Diagram of the VPC topology for the sealed enclave, including peering patterns and egress guards.
- Keystore/operator separation: confirmation of customer-managed KMS/HSM options and whether Redwood operators have any direct access to unencrypted tenant keys.
- Evidence of audit logs (where they live, retention, and format) and how we can ingest them during an audit.

Can you provide a short packet (PDFs + a diagram) and a one-page runbook for our security reviewers by EOD Tuesday (2025-06-17)? Also: who will be our internal Redwood contact for follow-ups?

Appreciate it — Lisa

--

Hi Lisa — attaching the packet we discussed. Summary answers below and attachments are appended as stubs.

Quick summary:
- Residency: For sealed-enclave private deployment we provision dedicated US-only nodes. No cross-region snapshot replication is enabled by default; customers may request controlled snapshots for DR with explicit written agreement. Attached: "SOC2-Type-II-Report-2024.pdf" and "residency-runbook-privatelink.pdf".
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS or HSM-mediated BYOK). Operators at Redwood do not have access to unencrypted tenant encryption keys; master keys are customer-controlled when BYOK is enabled. See "keystore-separation-matrix.xlsx" for the role matrix.
- Networking & VPC: Sealed-enclave topology uses a single-tenant VPC with dedicated peering/fibers where required. Egress filtering and NAT gateway rules are applied at the edge; default egress to internet is blocked. See "VPC-Sealed-Enclave-Diagram.png".
- Audit logs: All audit and operator actions are written to the customer's logging bucket (S3 in US region) and to our immutable append-only audit store for 13 months by default; longer retention can be configured. Logs are exportable in JSON/NDJSON for ingestion.

Attachments (stubs):
- SOC2-Type-II-Report-2024.pdf (redacted sections present)
- CAIQ-Response-Condensed-2025.pdf (focused answers)
- VPC-Sealed-Enclave-Diagram.png
- keystore-separation-matrix.xlsx
- residency-runbook-privatelink.pdf

Related: I created a Drive folder with raw diagrams and a live runbook for your engineers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFg

If you need expanded SIG answers or CAIQ detail cells, we can produce a full SIG workbook by EOD Thu (2025-06-19).

Thanks,

Irene / Sean — thanks for the fast turnaround, the packet looks good on first pass. A few follow-ups from our security reviewers:

1) Ephemeral keys & rotation: Can you confirm rotation cadence for ephemeral session keys used by the inference runtime and whether those ephemeral keys are derived from customer master keys or from Redwood-managed intermediate keys? We need a short statement to include in the risk register.
2) Audit log integrity: Are audit logs stamped with immutability checks (e.g., HMAC or tamper-evident chain)? If so, a one-paragraph description is sufficient.
3) Data export restriction: We need a simple redlined sentence confirming Redwood will not export training data, annotated content, or customer-provided corpora outside US nodes for this sealed-enclave deployment. Can you provide a single-sentence commitment for inclusion in our contract addendum?

Also — would you be available for a 30-minute sync on Wed 2025-06-18 10:00 PT to walk our security and infra folks through the runbook?

Best,
Lisa

Subject: Re: Sealed-enclave private deployment: residency & SIG/CAIQ evidence request

Hi Lisa — quick answers below and we've attached a short runbook excerpt and the keystore matrix for your redline.

1) Ephemeral keys & rotation: Ephemeral session keys used by the inference runtime are rotated every 4 hours by default. They are generated by the runtime and wrapped with the customer master key (BYOK) at the time of session creation; therefore ephemeral keys are not persisted unencrypted outside the sealed enclave. (See keystore-separation-matrix.xlsx for flow diagram).

2) Audit log integrity: Audit entries are appended to an immutable store and signed with an HMAC chain per-tenant. Each log batch is anchored with an HMAC that we publish to a tamper-evident ledger; customers may request periodic attestations.

3) Export restriction sentence for contract addendum (suggested): "Redwood Inference will not export customer training data, annotated datasets, or customer-provided corpora outside the United States for any sealed-enclave private deployment, except for snapshots explicitly authorized in writing by the customer for disaster recovery purposes."

We can do the Wed 2025-06-18 10:00 PT sync — I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda and include the runbook link: https://redwood.example.com/security/keystore-runbook

Next steps: Irene & Marissa will remain on thread for any technical clarifications; we can produce the full SIG workbook if your audit team wants deeper cell-level evidence by Thu.

Best,
Sean
